title: Navigating Tricks
intro: The shortest section in the book, and possibly the highest value per word. Getting the playhead and the view where you want them, instantly, is the difference between working and fiddling.

tips.d: Hold ⌃⌥ and drag a box around any part of the arrangement to zoom straight to it. Hold ⌃⌥ and click empty space to zoom back out.

tips.t: Know what the number keys actually do
tips.d: The top-row number keys recall screensets, not markers — Apple's guide says you recall a screenset by pressing any numeric key except 0, so 1–9 switch window layouts. If you want marker jumps on a key, open Key Commands (⌥K) and search “Go to Marker Number” — there are 20 of them, numbered by the order the markers appear in the project.

Open Key Commands with ⌥K and search “Selection”. Logic has several selection-based playback commands — Play from Selection is on ⇧Space by default and starts playback at the beginning of whatever you have selected — so you can audition just the part you are working on. Browse the list and put the one that matches your workflow on a key you can reach.

Two‑finger swipe left and right on a trackpad to move through the project. Apple documents gesture scrolling in the Tracks area, and dragging two fingers scrolls a pane horizontally as well as vertically — keep your hand off the scrollbar entirely.

tips.t: Use the Cycle area as a bookmark
tips.d: Select the region or passage you are working on and press U. Logic sets the left and right locators around it — rounded to bar lines — and turns Cycle on, so the yellow strip in the ruler marks your work area and keeps looping it. Use ⌘U instead if you want the locators exactly on the selection boundaries rather than rounded.

tips.t: Toggle Catch to stop the screen running away
tips.d: The Catch button makes the view follow the playhead. Click it off when you are doing detailed editing and the view will hold still while the song plays. You do not need to assign anything — Catch Playhead Position is already on the backquote (`) key, so you can toggle it without leaving the keyboard.
